title: The Water Cycle
seo_title: Grade 6 Water Cycle Worksheets: Evaporation, Condensation, Precipitation and Runoff
standard_text: Develop a model to describe the cycling of water through Earth’s systems driven by energy from the sun and the force of gravity.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on the water cycle (NGSS MS-ESS2-4): evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, runoff and infiltration, the roles of the sun and gravity, and labeled models. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: The sun and gravity drive the water cycle.
key_sub: Water evaporates, condenses into clouds, falls as precipitation, and flows or soaks back to the ocean, again and again.
body_html:
How to think about it

Water moves in a continuous cycle among the oceans, the atmosphere and the land. Energy from the sun and the pull of gravity drive it.

  • Evaporation: liquid water turns into water vapor and rises from oceans, lakes and puddles.
  • Transpiration: plants release water vapor from their leaves.
  • Condensation: water vapor cools and turns into tiny liquid droplets that form clouds.
  • Precipitation: water falls from clouds as rain, snow, sleet or hail.
  • Runoff: water flows over the land into streams, rivers and the ocean.
  • Infiltration: water soaks into the ground and becomes groundwater.
Example

What drives evaporation?

Liquid water needs energy to become a gas.

Answer: energy from the sun

Example

Drops form on a cold can. Which process?

Water vapor in the air cools.

Answer: condensation

Common mistakes

  • Thinking clouds are water vapor. They are liquid droplets or ice.
  • Thinking gravity causes evaporation. The sun does.
  • Thinking the water cycle has a start and an end.

Tiny droplets of liquid water or ice crystals that formed when water vapor cooled and condensed.

faq.q: What is the difference between runoff and infiltration?
faq.a: Runoff flows over the land into streams and rivers. Infiltration soaks into the ground and becomes groundwater.
